export default "## Custom views (optional)\n\nA script can draw its own editor element next to the knobs, store custom data and show live telemetry. The\nscript stays ONE file: the directive header, `class Processor` and one or more view classes.\n\nThe whole script runs twice: the Processor on the audio thread, every view class in its own sandboxed iframe\non the main thread. They share NO variables. Talk only through params, data and streams. A script that\ndeclares a view must keep its top level free of state: only `class`, `function` and `const NAME = ...` are\nallowed there (no `let`, no `var`, no top-level statements, no private static fields). Every top-level value\nis frozen. Create mutable things (typed arrays, Maps) in the constructor.\n\n### Declarations\n\n// @view [Class] <column> <row> <columns> <rows>\n    Places the class (default View) into the device panel grid. Cells are 3.5em squares in 3 rows, 1-based.\n    The knobs fill the remaining free cells. Example: 3 params fill column 1, so start the view at column 2.\n// @window [Class] <width> <height>\n    A resizable floating window in CSS pixels, opened from the device header or host.openWindow(name).\n// @collection <name> [count]\n// @field <name>.<field> [default] [min max type [unit]]   (the @param grammar)\n// @record <name> field=value ...                          (seed one record per line, instead of a count)\n    Persistent, undoable records the view edits and the processor reads.\n// @buffer <name> <length>\n    Persistent floats (a wavetable, a curve) the view writes and the processor reads.\n// @stream <name> <length> [value|ring|fft]\n    Processor to view telemetry (current step, scope, spectrum). Never saved, never rendered.\n// @param <name> ... [omit-default-ui]\n    The parameter gets no knob, the view is its only control. It stays automatable, modulatable and MIDI\n    learnable. Give its control host.attachParameter(element, name) so a right click opens the parameter menu.\n\n### Processor side\n\n- this.data.<name>: a frozen array of frozen records ({field: value}) per @collection, a Float32Array per\n  @buffer. Read only. Replaced on every change, read it where you need it.\n- dataChanged(name): called once after construction and after every change, between blocks. Rebuild derived\n  state here (a wavetable from partials), never allocate in process().\n- this.streams.<name>: value streams are a Float32Array you overwrite, ring and fft streams take\n  write(channel, s0, s1). `.active` is true while a view listens, skip the work otherwise.\n- message(data): called with every host.send(data) before the next process() call. Transient.\n\n### View side\n\nclass View {\n    constructor(host) { ... }   // build everything inside host.root\n    terminate() { }             // optional, the iframe is thrown away anyway, nothing needs cleaning up\n}\n\nhost.root, host.mode (\"inline\" | \"window\")\nhost.params.<name>: label, value, set(value), subscribe(observer),\n    sources, subscribeSources(observer)   (value includes automation and modulation, sources lists\n    \"automated\", \"modulated\", \"midi\", \"external\")\nhost.attachParameter(element, name, options?) -> {terminate()}   (right click on element opens the parameter menu,\n    {enterValue: true} adds a double click to type a value, for knobs and sliders, not for checkboxes)\nhost.data.<collection>: length, get(index), toArray(), set(index, {field: value}), insert(index, values?),\n    remove(index), subscribe(observer)\nhost.data.<buffer>: length, get(index), toArray(), set(values, offset?), subscribe(observer)\nhost.streams.<name>.subscribe(observer)   (fft streams arrive as magnitudes)\nhost.edit(procedure)                      (all writes inside become ONE undo step)\nhost.gesture() -> {edit(procedure), end()} (a drag: live edits, ONE undo step at the end)\nhost.preview.noteOn(pitch, velocity?), host.preview.noteOff(pitch)\nhost.send(data), host.openWindow(name?), host.closeWindow(name?)\nhost.color(name, opacity?)\n\nA write outside edit or gesture is its own undo step, like a knob click. Use a gesture for every drag.\n\n### Design guide (match the stock devices)\n\nThe view must look like it was always part of openDAW. Derived from the stock device displays:\n\n1. Frame: the studio adds no frame, the view draws its own like the stock displays. On host.root set\n   box-sizing border-box, padding 4px, a 0.5px border in host.color(\"displayGrid\", 0.12) and an 8px radius.\n   Keep the frame 1px inside the page (margin 1px, width and height calc(100% - 2px)): at a fractional\n   browser zoom the outermost pixel of a view can be cut off. Round the canvas 4px. Background transparent,\n   the device panel shows through.\n2. Colours: draw data with host.color(\"displayStroke\", opacity), never with arbitrary colours.\n   - main curve: opacity 0.75 to 1.0\n   - secondary curves and handles: 0.4 to 0.5\n   - reference lines (zero, threshold): 0.25, dashed setLineDash([2, 2])\n   - area under a curve: a vertical gradient from displayStroke at 0.2 to 0.3 down to transparent\n   - grid lines: host.color(\"displayGrid\", 0.12)\n   - selection or a playing step: a faint fill, displayStroke at 0.03 to 0.1\n   Studio accent colours (blue, orange, green, purple) only for small state marks, never for large areas.\n3. Lines: 1 CSS pixel. Scale the context by devicePixelRatio once, then use lineWidth = 1.\n4. Text: inherit the font (Rubik, 11px). Scale labels 8 to 9px in white at 0.2 opacity. No new fonts, no bold.\n5. Canvas size: let CSS size the canvas (width and height 100%, min-height 0, grid rows minmax(0, 1fr)), then\n   in a ResizeObserver set canvas.width/height = clientWidth/Height × devicePixelRatio and redraw. Never let the\n   drawing size feed back into the layout.\n6. Redraw on change only: from subscribe callbacks and the ResizeObserver. No free-running animation loop\n   unless a stream is drawn, then draw in the stream callback.\n7. Interaction: pointer events with setPointerCapture, touch-action none, a clear cursor (ew-resize, crosshair).\n   Keep the hit areas generous. Every drag is a host.gesture(), every click a single write.\n8. Compact: the panel is 3 rows of 3.5em. Show what the sound does (a curve, a pattern, a spectrum), leave\n   numbers to the knobs. Keep the view narrow, 4 to 6 columns: small devices are easier to read and to handle\n   in the device chain. Put large editing into a @window instead of widening the view.\n\n### Pitfalls (mistakes that already happened, avoid them)\n\n1. Empty data as \"use the default\": if a script treats an all-zero @buffer (or an empty @collection) as \"use a\n   built-in default\", the FIRST partial edit must store the whole default first (in the same edit), then the\n   change. Otherwise everything outside the edited range becomes silence.\n2. Write only what changed: during a drag call `host.data.<buffer>.set(values, offset)` with just the touched\n   range, never the whole buffer per pointer move. Every write is kept in the undo history and sent to the\n   engine.\n3. Parameters jump once per block: a param that selects or morphs between shapes (table position, waveform,\n   morph) must be smoothed per sample (a few milliseconds), or fast moves and automation click.\n4. Interpolate properly: read tables with 4-point Hermite (or better) and crossfade between neighbouring frames,\n   linear lookups sound grainy when scanning.\n5. Guard degenerate values: `Math.round` on an int param can give 0, a division by a count can become a\n   division by zero. Clamp every value you divide by or index with (at least 1, inside the table). A single NaN\n   silences the device.\n6. Deterministic processor: never use Math.random() in the Processor for anything audible that must render the\n   same offline (an export) as live. Random generators belong in the view, their result stored as data.\n7. Canvas feedback: never size the layout from the canvas you draw (grid rows minmax(0, 1fr), min-height 0),\n   or the view grows with every redraw.\n8. Stacked or 3D drawings: draw lines with opacity fading by depth, never fill the area under each line to hide\n   the ones behind. Overlapping fills create dark patches that look broken.\n9. Buttons must say what they change: group buttons by their target (\"Fill all frames\", \"Selected frames\"),\n   explain the hovered button in a hint line, confirm what happened. A button that silently replaces all data\n   is a surprise. Make selections (a frame, a range) explicit and visible.\n10. Discoverable windows: a @window needs a visible button in the inline view (not only a double-click) and\n    a short hint how to open it.\n11. Fresh data: host.data.<buffer>.toArray() returns a copy. Re-read it in the subscribe callback instead of\n    keeping an old array, or a reopened view or another view's edit shows stale data.\n"
